---
name: cds-development
description: Implement, change, or analyze ABAP CDS data definitions and their dependencies or consumers. Use for DDLS and CDS modeling tasks.

# CDS development

**Workspace preflight.** Whenever this workflow edits or hands off serialized CDS/ABAP sources in a workspace, run `LintABAPProject` (`lint_abap_project`) before sending changes to SAP; if unavailable, report the skipped preflight and use caller-supplied `LintABAP` if available for ABAP sources. Confirm the configured root is the intended project (`SAP_AI_DEV_TOOLKIT_WORKSPACE_ROOT`, or the MCP process working directory by default; `directory` is relative to that root), `targetRelease` matches the SAP target, `dependencies.missingFolders` and `syntaxRules.disabled` are empty, and `status` is `clean`. `issues`, `incomplete`, `no-abap-files`, or a mismatched root/release are not passes. This is static analysis only and does not validate SAP activation or runtime; caller-supplied `LintABAP` on the latest source for the exact object set remains mandatory immediately before activation. Skip when no serialized project source exists.

## Tool shortlist

Query the active MCP server's live `tools/list` once; use task-relevant tools with their returned schemas. Locate views and usages with `SearchObject` and `GrepObjects`; read DDLS with `GetSource`; compare workspace and SAP versions with `CompareSource`; use `GetCDSDependencies` for upstream dependencies, `GetCDSImpactAnalysis` for consumers, and `GetCDSElementInfo` for element metadata. Trace references with `FindReferences`; edit via `EditSource` / `WriteSource`. Validate with `SyntaxCheck`, `RunATCCheck`, activation via `Activate` / `ActivateMultiple`, and read-only runtime queries via `RunQuery` or `GetTableContents` when exposed. Tool names shown in PascalCase (such as `GetSource` or `LintABAP`) are logical names; the live MCP surface exposes them as lowercase snake_case. A server scoped to a single destination (the normal case for generated `mcp.json` entries) exposes them unprefixed, so `GetSource` appears as `get_source` and `LintABAP` as `lint_abap`; when several destinations share one server, each name is destination-prefixed with its slug for disambiguation (for example `cfd_run_query`). Always call the exact names returned by `tools/list`.

For a new transparent DDIC table backing a CDS entity, use live `CreateTable`; it is not for CDS views. It writes generated DDL and activates in one SAP call, so require explicit approval and a known package/transport. It does not create authorization objects; transport release/deletion is unavailable through this addon.

## Language level and naming

For DDLS/CDS source, establish the target CDS language level and capabilities, plus the oldest CDS level required by consumers. Do not infer CDS syntax support solely from an ABAP release; validate against the target's CDS capability or syntax check. For accompanying ABAP code, identify the oldest supported ABAP release and, on ABAP 7.40 or newer, actively consider modern ABAP syntax while checking each feature's minimum release. Use descriptive business/domain names for CDS entities and elements, following required SAP and project conventions. Apply Clean ABAP naming to ABAP identifiers where applicable; see the [Clean ABAP Cheat Sheet](https://github.com/SAP/styleguides/blob/main/clean-abap/cheat-sheet/CheatSheet.md) and [Names section](https://github.com/SAP/styleguides/blob/main/clean-abap/CleanABAP.md#names).

1. Inspect the target DDLS source, its existing data definitions, package conventions, dependencies, and consumers before editing.
2. Use live `GetCDSDependencies`, `GetCDSImpactAnalysis`, and `GetCDSElementInfo` tools when exposed to understand upstream sources, downstream impact, and element metadata. Use their current live names and schemas.
3. Implement only the requested CDS behavior. Validate the changed definition, affected dependencies, and relevant consumers with operations actually exposed by the system; report unavailable analysis or validation capabilities rather than inferring results.
4. CDS changes require executable validation, not only syntax. Do not treat syntax, ATC, or activation as substitutes for behavior evidence. After activation, query or otherwise consume the changed view/entity with representative filters and projections using `RunQuery` or `GetTableContents` when available. Prefer safe real rows from the target system; if no suitable data exists, use authorized isolated sample data or document the lack of executable data. Verify returned fields, computed expressions, casts, currencies/units, parameters, associations exposed to consumers, key semantics, annotations relevant to consumers, authorization-relevant behavior when testable, and empty-result behavior.
5. For CDS logic that is consumed by ABAP classes, RAP behavior, or services, add or update an automated test around the consumer or a focused ABAP Unit test that selects from the CDS artifact with controlled input. Use test doubles or isolated fixture data when available/authorized. If the MCP server only allows live read-only queries, record the exact validation query, input data source, row count, and observed result as the CDS runtime test evidence. Before activating CDS or related ABAP code, `LintABAP` must succeed on the latest source of every ABAP code object in the exact activation request (including dependencies); re-lint after any source change. If lint is unavailable, fails, source is missing, or findings remain unresolved, do not activate and report the blocker. For `ActivateMultiple`, activate only the exact reviewed and linted object set, not a broad inactive-object/package list. Check pending inactive objects with `GetInactiveObjects`, activate authorized CDS changes in dependency order, and treat activation failure as a blocker. Never activate merely to run tests.
